The paper compares four theoretical RCS prediction methods: Chu, Tai, Van Vleck, and Ufimtsev against experimental data
Primary experimental measurement used a 2.48 m copper wire at 450 MHz (λ = 2/3 m) with kℓ = 11.7
Wire radius was 4 × 10⁻⁴ m (15.8 mil), giving ka = 3.78 × 10⁻³
Measurement accuracy was within 1 dB for calibration and ±1 degree for angular measurements
Seven datasets with kℓ values from 4.44 to 45.7 were analyzed
Chu's expression is accurate only near broadside incidence (θ ≈ 90°) but fails at other angles
Tai's original expression had an asymptotic error at broadside that was corrected by introducing function f(θ)
Modified Tai's expression provides accurate predictions within ±few dB for 4.5 < kℓ < 17
Modified Tai's expression fails for kℓ ≥ 45.7, with errors exceeding 10 dB
Van Vleck's expressions show good agreement with data except at end-on incidence
Van Vleck's predictions differ from data by within 4 dB at peaks and 2-3 degrees in look angle
Ufimtsev's solution provides the most accurate predictions across all kℓ values tested
Ufimtsev's expressions are complex but offer comparable accuracy to Van Vleck with better end-on performance
BRACT computer program achieves agreement with experiment within ±1 dB for all reliable data
BRACT uses the Source Distribution Integral (SDI) technique to solve thin wire integral equations
BRACT is coded in FORTRAN IV for Control Data Computing System execution
Circular polarization RCS is 6 dB below linear polarization RCS
Experimental RCS measurement accuracy degrades at nulls compared to peaks
Lincoln Laboratory data showed some errors up to the first null
Avco experimental data contained several decibels of error due to experimental difficulties
The paper identifies that Van Vleck's method is more generally valid than previously credited
Resonant wire conditions (kℓ = nπ/2) are excluded from the theoretical analysis
The correction function f(θ) ensures modified Tai's expression reduces to Chu's at broadside
Seven different experimental sources provided data across the kℓ range studied
The research was conducted from December 1971 through September 1972 at The Aerospace Corporation
